documents.unit: Instructional Design and Delivery (AI in Higher Education)
documents.title: AI Guides and Resources for Students: Asking the Right Questions: A Student Guide to Responsible AI Use in College
documents.stance_why: The guide states "Each faculty member sets their own expectations for AI use in their course. Some may permit it in limited ways; others may prohibit it entirely." It sets no university rule and sends students to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: Student-facing guide urging reflective AI use. It says each instructor sets expectations and students should ask when unsure. It lists questions to ask about permitted uses, disclosure and AI-free work.

units.why: The guide says heavy reliance "can hinder your personal growth", a reason AI use is limited because doing the work yourself builds skill; fits P41, general rationale, informs.
units.anchor: relying on them too heavily can hinder your personal growth
units.frag_start: While AI tools can be helpful

units.why: "When AI writes your arguments, solves your problems, or reflects for you, it undermines the very skills" states outsourcing practice undermines skill; P41 not P19 because it explains rather than bans.
units.anchor: When AI writes your arguments, solves your problems, or reflects for you
units.frag_start: While AI tools can be helpful

documents.unit: Information Technology Services / Office of Information Security
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Guidelines
documents.stance_why: The page gives data-protection rules and an approved tool list, not a stance on AI in coursework: it says "We urge caution when using external AI systems" and approves tools for Gonzaga data. No ban or encouragement of learning use, so delegates.
documents.summary: Information Security guidance on generative AI covering data privacy, an approved-tools table, verification of output, bias, and a glossary. It applies to data under the IT Use Policy rather than to coursework rules.

units.why: The office "is committed to providing guidance on the ethical and responsible use of generative" AI, a university-level purpose statement (P56).
units.anchor: committed to providing guidance on the ethical and responsible use of generative Artificial Intelligence

units.why: "our guidelines will continue to evolve" says the guidelines are provisional (P54).
units.anchor: our guidelines will continue to evolve

units.why: "We urge caution when using external AI systems" advises care with tools lacking university-grade security; P50 (protect data, prefer managed tools).
units.anchor: We urge caution when using external AI systems

units.why: "Lower paid tiers and free tiers are usually NOT sandboxed." explains which tools protect data (P50).
units.anchor: Lower paid tiers and free tiers are usually NOT sandboxed.

units.why: Defines "Sandboxed" as the vendor not using uploaded data in its training model, a definition that sets scope for the approved list (P61).
units.anchor: Sandboxed means that the company/org will not use data uploaded into their AI training model.

units.why: Use of AI with Gonzaga data "must be made with an AI tool that has been fully approved" through contract review and managed by ITS; P50 (vetted tools) fits better than P65 because it binds users, not procurement.
units.anchor: must be made with an AI tool that has been fully approved
units.frag_start: The use of the AI tools with Gonzaga data

units.why: The approved list shows Microsoft Copilot when logged in with Gonzaga SSO as approved for Gonzaga data, a sanctioned tool (P17).
units.anchor: Microsoft Copilot (when logged in using Gonzaga SSO)
units.frag_start: Microsoft Copilot (when logged in using Gonzaga SSO)

units.why: The list marks "All other NON-sandboxed AI" as not approved, ruling out those tools for Gonzaga data (P50).
units.anchor: All other NON-sandboxed AI

units.why: "The restrictions above only apply to data covered by Gonzaga's IT Use Policy" sets the scope of the list (P61).
units.anchor: only apply to data covered by Gonzaga's IT Use Policy

units.why: PII, PHI or other sensitive data "should not be uploaded or processed" on unapproved platforms; protects personal data (P50).
units.anchor: should not be uploaded or processed on platforms not approved

units.why: "Generative AIs often integrate all input they receive, including prompts" warns tools keep prompts, a privacy fact (P50).
units.anchor: Generative AIs often integrate all input they receive
units.frag_start: Generative AIs often integrate all input

units.why: "You should only provide prompts and other data meant for public sharing." restricts what is entered into AI (P50).
units.anchor: You should only provide prompts and other data meant for public sharing.

units.why: Notes providers show "varying degrees of respect for authorial rights", a concern on authors' rights in AI training (P52).
units.anchor: varying degrees of respect for authorial rights among providers
units.frag_start: Generative AIs also collect extensive data

units.why: "it can sometimes yield inaccurate information that appears credible, potentially fabricating sources" says AI output may be wrong (P31).
units.anchor: sometimes yield inaccurate information that appears credible
units.frag_start: Generative AI systems create text by forecasting

units.why: "It is essential to verify the accuracy of any information utilized." tells users to verify AI output (P31).
units.anchor: It is essential to verify the accuracy of any information utilized.
units.frag_start: Our mission calls for a mature commitment

units.why: "Generative AIs mirror and can magnify biases" names bias harm to marginalized communities (P53).
units.anchor: Generative AIs mirror and can magnify biases
units.frag_start: Generative AIs mirror and can magnify

units.why: "We encourage our community to approach AI with a discerning mindset" states institutional principles for AI use (P56).
units.anchor: We encourage our community to approach AI with a discerning mindset

units.why: Defines "Artificial intelligence" as a computer system imitating humans in some ways; sets what the guidelines cover (P61).
units.anchor: Artificial intelligence is basically a super-smart computer system
units.frag_end: typically require human intelligence and time.

units.why: Defines "Generative AI" as using large language models to make new text, images, code (P61).
units.anchor: Generative AI leverages the power of large language models to make new things

units.why: Defines "Large language models" and how they work (P61).
units.anchor: Large language models, or LLMs, use machine learning techniques

units.anchor: It's a field of computer science, under the umbrella of AI
units.frag_start: If artificial intelligence is the goal
units.frag_end: as computer hardware has become faster, smaller, more powerful and better able to process all that information.

units.why: Defines "Hallucinations" as fabricated responses; kept as definition P61 rather than P31 since it is a glossary entry.
units.anchor: they can give inaccurate responses that developers refer to as hallucinations

units.why: Defines "Responsible AI", stating systems "can reflect any inherent biases" (P61 as glossary entry).
units.anchor: Responsible AI guides people as they try to design systems that are safe and fair

units.why: Defines "Prompts" as instructions given to an AI (P61).

documents.unit: Instructional Design and Delivery (AI in Higher Education)
documents.title: AI Guides and Resources for Faculty
documents.stance_why: The page describes a Faculty AI Use Guide with "High Value," "Some Value," and "Negative Value" categories for AI uses, and leaves course decisions to instructors. It is a tiered guide, so delegates with tiers.
documents.summary: Landing page for faculty resources: a linked Faculty AI Use Guide (not captured) categorizing uses by value to learning, videos on integrity, writing and hallucinations, and library and teaching-center support.

units.why: Says "human teachers - especially at Gonzaga - have the greater impact", a principle that AI does not replace instructors (P56).
units.anchor: human teachers

units.why: The guide "supports instructors in using AI thoughtfully to enhance learning, uphold academic integrity", an instructor-facing statement of purpose (P56).
